title: Preserve sample and component axes throughout Riemannian EM
body:
## Problem

A one-component fit loses its component axis when the updated mean is squeezed. Separately, `dist_broadcast` can take its elementwise shortcut when the sample and component counts coincide, instead of producing all sample/component distances. These shape errors break density evaluation and variance updates for valid small mixtures.

## Change

Keep the batch mean's component axis. Centralize component distances in a helper that explicitly broadcasts and flattens sample/component pairs before calling the metric, then restores the `(n_samples, n_components)` result. Use it in both density methods and the variance update. Flattening also respects metrics whose vectorization helpers expect one batch axis.

## Validation

The same 13 regression/control cases on unchanged base `2fc8e25eb8955767292552f9c0c1438be362ba8f` report **10 failures and 3 passes** on both NumPy and Autograd. They cover actual random/k-means initialized fits, a single observation, one component, equal sample/component counts, 2→1→2 refits, and analytic Poincaré-diameter mean/density oracles.

At source `324ecd6e21f24bb64caf6505b3276535f9b8b293`, all learning tests plus Euclidean and Poincaré geometry tests, excluding the existing slow/redundant markers, report:

- NumPy: **759 passed, 5 skipped, 362 deselected, 5 xfailed, 4 xpassed**.
- Autograd: **761 passed, 3 skipped, 362 deselected, 4 xfailed, 5 xpassed**.
- Ruff and applicable pre-commit hooks pass; the validated checkout remains clean.

[Exact-source CI](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43672411380). Python 3.13.18, NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1 and Autograd 1.9.1. The full repository and PyTorch backend were not run.

## Scope and related work

This fixes sample/component shape handling. It does not change posterior normalization or batch-weight scaling. Reviewed the existing EM implementation and initialization history, including #564 and #841, all six prior author PRs, and the EM source at all 50 pre-existing fork heads; none contains this axis repair.
